narrative:
The model determined that you have a 45% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the length of the loan you requested. Your credit history had the strongest influence and pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. You have no previous credits or have paid everything off, a situation that is quite rare. Among approved applicants, 57% have a solid record of existing credits that were paid on time and another 33% show critical but ultimately repaid credits. The absence of any positive repayment track record made the model considerably less confident in your ability to repay.

The status of your checking account was the second most important factor and also increased the likelihood of being seen as higher risk. Your account balance sits between 0 and 200 DM, a range held by only 18% of approved applicants, while nearly 60% of successful applicants have no checking account at all or maintain stronger balances.

The requested loan duration worked in your favor. At 12 months it is well below the 19-month average of approved loans, which helped pull the prediction back toward approval. Unfortunately, these positive aspects were not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your credit history and checking account status.

You should focus on building a clear repayment history on smaller commitments, aim to keep a healthier checking balance, and consider applying again in 6–12 months with a stronger track record.
